dedupe_keys.name: dynamic state and parameter estimation for natural gas pipeline networks from scada data

description: This method by Kaarthik Sundar and Anatoly Zlotnik, presented at the 3rd IEEE Conference on Control Technology and Applications (2019), estimates the state and parameters of natural gas pipeline networks, in which pressures and flows depend on time-varying injections, withdrawals and compressor controls. Coverage: the estimation is posed as an optimal control problem constrained by coupled partial differential equations on each pipe for space- and time-dependent density and mass flux, discretised with nodal conditions into nonlinear least squares problems, with a rapid, scalable method that handles measurement and process noise. It is evaluated on a data set from a capacity planning model of an actual pipeline system and one month of time series from that system's supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) system. Format and access: an arXiv preprint with a PDF. Licence and cost: free to read; no licence stated on the abstract page. Caveats: the operator and data are not named, and code is not mentioned on the abstract page. The method can underpin a gas network digital twin that tracks line pack and flows from SCADA for network flow and optimisation studies. It relates to GasModels.jl and GasLib in the catalogue.
